clue.text: Mediterranean city hall, active in fits and starts

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their opening letters, so take the first letter of each word from hall to and

explanation.surface: A busy port's town hall works only sporadically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fits and starts' reads as a single phrase meaning sporadically, but only 'starts' is the signal; 'in', 'fits' and 'and' give letters along with 'hall' and 'active'.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is a port city on Israel's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Stormy water causing damage without moving?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: causing damage means harming

indicators.note: stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters of water are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A storm at sea does harm without anything shifting?
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. 'moving' looks like travelling, which the surface's 'without moving' plays on, but it means touching.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heartwarming is emotionally touching, which is what moving means here.

clue.text: Writer named Christopher Robin's home after one

indicators.note: after places the forest's name after the numeral for one

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
Sherwood Forest is the home of Robin Hood

explanation.surface: Seems to name A. A. Milne's Christopher Robin and his home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christopher Robin' looks like one name from Winnie-the-Pooh, but the clue splits there: Christopher belongs to the definition and Robin is Robin Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was the English novelist of Goodbye to Berlin.

clue.text: Resort to USA for transport

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort, sort again, so the letters of to and USA are rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning to America for one's means of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a noun or 'turn to', but is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Autos are cars, a means of transport.

clue.text: Make a fuss about the centre of Dartmouth — a Devonshire speciality

indicators.note: about puts the fuss word around the middle letter of the town's name

parts.note: to create is to make a fuss

indicators.note: the centre of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter

explanation.surface: Kicking up a fuss in the middle of a Devon port, home of a local delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M (the centre of Dartmouth) inside CREATE. A cream tea is scones with jam and clotted cream, a speciality of Devon, the English county where Dartmouth is.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea, scones served with jam and clotted cream, is famously associated with Devon.

clue.text: Tin-opener that is gripping top of lid, as in song

parts.note: a tin is a can
a tab is a ring-pull, the opener on a drinks can

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Describes a can with a ring-pull that clutches the lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' puts L (top of lid) inside IE. 'Tin-opener' looks like one tool but splits into tin and opener.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantabile is a musical direction meaning in a smooth, singing style.

clue.text: Genuine resident of Liechtenstein

indicators.note: a resident of a place lives inside it, so the letters sit within the country's name

explanation.surface: Asks for a true citizen of a tiny Alpine principality.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loanword meaning authentic or real.

clue.text: Prepared to be out to lunch before daybreak?

parts.note: out to lunch is slang for crazy, mad
ere is an old word for before
read as day broken: the letters of day rearranged

explanation.surface: Ready to go crazy before dawn?
explanation.walkthrough: 'daybreak' looks like dawn, but is read as DAY broken up into ADY. 'to be' just links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Made ready is a phrase meaning got prepared, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Spooky canoe's back on lake

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Eerie scene of a canoe's stern on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and frightening, the same as spooky.

clue.text: Guess one's delighted to have a drink?

definitions.meaning: a guess made with no information to go on

definitions.text: one's delighted to have a drink?
definitions.meaning: read de-lighted as having the lights removed: someone downing a drink with the lights off

explanation.walkthrough: 'delighted' looks like pleased, but is read as de-lighted, lights out; a shot is a small measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild guess made without any knowledge is proverbially a stab in the dark.

clue.text: Variation in phone call — it's not uniform

indicators.note: a variation in something changes its form, so the letters of phone call and it's are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as its letters ITS

explanation.surface: A remark that a telephone call that varies is not standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variation in' rearranges PHONECALLITS; 'it's' is fodder, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain clothes are ordinary civilian dress worn by detectives instead of uniform.

clue.text: Blind prophet bores one, as you may see

parts.note: to bore someone is to tire them
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A blind seer is tedious, as you might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you may see' just links; it nods ironically at the prophet's blindness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresias is the blind seer of Thebes in Greek myth.

clue.text: Blair, alternatively? Fancy that!

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
well! is an exclamation of surprise, like fancy that!

explanation.surface: Seems to wonder about Tony Blair, with a cry of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' looks like Tony Blair, the former British prime minister; it is Eric Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of the writer Eric Arthur Blair.

clue.text: Plentiful gain, possibly, over the border

indicators.note: over means covering, so the reworked letters go around the other piece
possibly signals the letters of gain can be arranged another way

parts.note: a bound is a limit or boundary, a border

explanation.surface: Lots to be gained, perhaps, by crossing the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the border' reads like crossing a frontier; 'over' is a container signal, the reworked letters of gain lying over and around the border word.
explanation.definitionFit: Abounding means existing in great quantity, so it is a synonym of plentiful.

clue.text: Instrument making snout feel funny

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of snout and feel are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that leaves the nose feeling peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose flute is a wind instrument blown through the nostrils.

clue.text: Get round old boy — fancy old mediator

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word get goes around the other piece

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
ween is an archaic verb meaning think or suppose, to fancy

explanation.surface: Advice to dodge an old schoolmate, a fancy old go-between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective describing the old boy, but 'fancy old' is the archaic verb ween.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between carries messages between parties, which is the role of a mediator.

clue.text: Very musical overtures from Arthur Sullivan — such as Iolanthe

indicators.note: an overture opens a work, so take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Praises Sullivan's overtures, such as the one to Iolanthe, as very musical.
explanation.walkthrough: Iolanthe is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, so 'overtures' fits the scene but signals first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian musical direction meaning very, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Steve is in trouble, being easily upset

indicators.note: in trouble, the letters of Steve is in are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Steve, in a fix, is touchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is fodder, not part of the phrase 'in trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensitive person is quickly hurt or offended, easily upset.

clue.text: Note about deplorable king

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for deplorable is read backwards

parts.note: sad can mean pitiful, deplorable

explanation.surface: A message about a lamentable monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written message, but is a musical note. King Midas turned all he touched to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas was the legendary king of Phrygia with the golden touch.

clue.text: Starting to develop shot by incomer

indicators.note: shot as in shot to pieces, so the letters of by and incomer are scrambled

explanation.surface: A newcomer fires the first shot of a growing plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a gunshot, but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Embryonic means at an early stage, only beginning to develop.

clue.text: Small number, then large number, start to fall asleep

parts.note: No. is the short form of number
D is the Roman numeral for 500
the off is the start of a race, as in from the off

explanation.surface: Counting small then big numbers as you begin to drop off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to fall asleep' reads as one phrase; 'start' gives OFF and 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod off is to drift into sleep, a synonym of fall asleep.

clue.text: Scott's ship lacks very popular dance music

indicators.note: lacks means is without, so a piece is taken out of the ship's name

parts.note: Discovery was the ship of Captain Scott's first Antarctic expedition

explanation.surface: A famous polar ship missing something; then a dance style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very popular' looks like a phrase, but 'very' is what is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is a genre of popular dance music of the 1970s.

clue.text: Empty apartment rented by head of Iberian company for Madrid players

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: let means rented out

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An empty flat let to a Spanish firm's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Atlético Madrid is a Spanish football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlético Madrid is a football club, so its team are Madrid players.

clue.text: Composer showing musical aptitude, looking outside in?

indicators.note: in places the edge letters of looking within the other piece

parts.note: to have an ear is to have musical aptitude

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A composer showing musical talent, peering in from outside?
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking outside in' suggests an onlooker peering in; it splits into two signals, one picking the outer letters, one placing them within.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: Hidden danger in role reversal

indicators.note: reversal means the word for role is written backwards

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Danger lurking in a switch of roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a concealed hazard waiting to catch someone.

clue.text: Bad guys in leathers, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters of guys in leathers are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Bikers in leather jackets as villains, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like the idiom 'so to speak'; the second 'in' links. Estuary English is the accent of London and the Thames estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Estuary English is a type of accent, a manner of speaking from south-east England.

clue.text: Find me filling in voucher

indicators.note: filling in means occupying the interior, so the word me goes inside

parts.note: a coupon is a voucher

explanation.surface: Filling in a voucher form with one's details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling in' looks like completing a form, but is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon something is to find it by chance.

clue.text: Birds share nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of share go haywire

explanation.surface: Birds dividing up their nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheas are large flightless South American birds.
